title: codex-ux findings
description: Response shape for a UX delegation. Passed to `codex exec --output-schema`; the model's final message conforms to this instead of to prose instructions.

surfaces_covered.description: The user-facing surfaces actually reviewed — screen, flow, or component names, each with the path it was read from.

findings.description: Issues in what the user encounters. Empty is a valid answer; do not pad.

surface.description: Which screen, flow, or component this belongs to.

file.description: Repo-relative path. Must be a file you actually read.

now.description: What the user experiences today — quote the actual string or describe the actual behavior the code produces.

problem.description: Who it hurts and how. A problem no user has is not a finding.

suggest.description: Concrete replacement copy or behavior. Actual text, not 'improve the wording' — a vague suggestion is a rejected finding.

kind.description: Which category of user-facing problem this is.

objective.description: true when the issue is checkable against a rule (missing input label, raw exception shown to the user, destructive action with no confirmation). false when it is a judgment call about tone, wording, or emphasis. The caller sorts on this — do not blur the two.

inconclusive.description: Places where the source does not determine what the user actually sees — dynamic content, theming, or rendering you cannot resolve by reading. Report here instead of guessing at rendered output.

notes.description: What limited the pass: missing product context, absent voice or terminology rules, surfaces deliberately skipped. Empty string if none.
